thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: P1 alert fired PD-az2-nic-degrade — 5xx surge and node NIC errors in az2, auto-prefailover candidates flagged. See link: https://pd.redwood.example/alerts/PD-az2-nic-degrade :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Alert details: service=serving-runtime, symptom=5xx+latency, impacted_shards=az2-* , escalation_policy=oncall-az2 -> network-oncall

Sam Nguyen: acked — I'm oncall, grabbing the runbook. @network-oncall can you look now?

Priya Kapoor: noticed increased kvcache evictions and `prefixcache_corruption` logs around 14:02 UTC. Pushing a metrics snapshot to the incident channel.

Jorge Alvarez: putting initial mitigation plan: 1) slow-redirect 30% traffic az2->az3 2) increase eviction bounds 3) start provider ticket if NIC hardware shows errors.

Sam Nguyen: executing step 1 now — applying routing patch to redirect.
```bash
# apply traffic redirect canary
redwoodctl route update --from az2 --to az3 --percent 30 --reason "pd:az2 nic degrade canary redirect"
```

deploy-bot: route update accepted: job_id=job_20260315_1430, state=rolling

Priya Kapoor: customer impact estimate: approx 9% of requests from EU region hitting az2 saw 5xx. Top affected customers: acct-1253, acct-8890. Support notified.

network-oncall: investigating fabric metrics — seeing RX errors and NIC resets on 7 hosts in az2 rack-5. Suspect upstream switch flap. Opening provider case now.

Jorge Alvarez: bumping redirect to 70% per runbook step 2 to reduce error surface. Will keep 30% as warm backfill policy.

Sam Nguyen: applied 70% redirect. Observability: errors dropped from 18%->5% within 90s. Latency still elevated for in-flight sessions.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation: PD escalated to network-oncall at +12m; oncall acknowledged.

network-oncall: provider confirmed intermittent fabric unstable, they are rehoming traffic and replacing switch. ETA 18-30 mins. Continuing monitoring.

Priya Kapoor: opening incident doc and incident-notes: https://confluence.redwood/incident/PD-az2-2026-03-15 — adding mitigation timeline and customer list.

Sam Nguyen: started rolling fallback activation for critical customers only (enterprise-tier). Config snippet:
```json
{"priority_policy":"enterprise-first","redirect":true,"drain_seconds":60}
```

Jorge Alvarez: initiated canary fallback: enterprise customers diverted fully to az3, general traffic 70%. Observability: enterprise error rate -> 0.4% now. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: fallback activation completed for enterprise group, job_id=fbk_519876_01

Priya Kapoor: support: sending proactive comms to affected customers, created 6 support tickets and flagged potential SLAs. Copying CSMs.

Sam Nguyen: monitoring console — KV cache warmups causing transient latency; expected to stabilize after warmup period (~8-12m).

network-oncall: provider reports partial remediation; NIC resets have stopped on 5 of 7 hosts, continuing work on remaining 2.

Jorge Alvarez: lowering redirect to 50% to test recovery while avoiding thrash. Will watch error budget.

Sam Nguyen: note to PD: incident acknowledged -> mitigation in place, provider engaged, partial fallback/reroute active. Marking incident as 'active-mitigated'.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: if error rate stays below 1% for 10 minutes, consider handing back to monitoring and closing.

Priya Kapoor: error rate has held ~0.6% for 12m; logs show no new prefixcache_corruption. Support updates queued.

Sam Nguyen: handing off to post-incident followup: will keep routing at 25% redirect for 30m then revert if stable. Creating followup ticket for infra to replace remaining NICs.

network-oncall: provider set a maintenance window to replace switch in 22 mins; we have a tracking case number.

Jorge Alvarez: preparing rollback playbook in case we see regression when moving traffic back.

Sam Nguyen: closing the page in PD — mitigation stable, customers notified, followups created. Final status: mitigated, partial fallback, provider replacement scheduled. Thanks all. :raised_hands:

incident-bot: Incident thread closed by Sam Nguyen — summary: PD-az2-nic-degrade mitigated via regional redirect and provider remediation. Follow-up owners: network-oncall (provider work), infra (replace nics), support (customer outreach).
